documents.title: Guiding Principles for Everyone
documents.summary: Campus-wide principles for all AI users at UNO, grouped under integrity, transparency, access and AI literacy. They cover data privacy, verification of output, bias, disclosure, equitable access and training, and set no course-level rule.
documents.stance_why: The page lists community-wide principles on integrity, transparency, access and literacy, e.g. 'Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated' and 'Refrain from inputting personal or confidential information'. It neither bans AI nor leaves the decision to instructors, and it assumes AI use under conditions, so permit.

units.why: Imperative 'Refrain from inputting personal or confidential information into AI tools' protects personal data, so it is a privacy rule for everyone (P50).
units.anchor: Refrain from inputting personal or confidential information into AI tools.

units.why: 'Ensure all AI tools are used in accordance with risk classification and security and FERPA' ties AI use to existing law and university security policy, which is P77 rather than P50 because it points to the external rules, not data protection itself.
units.anchor: Ensure all AI tools are used in accordance with risk classification and security and FERPA

units.why: 'Ensure all data is deidentified' when using an AI tool is a data-protection requirement (P50).
units.anchor: Ensure all data is deidentified when using in an AI tool.

units.why: 'human oversight ... to verify accuracy and minimize bias' tells users to check AI output; P31 fits better than P73 because it concerns content accuracy, not decisions about people.
units.anchor: Provide human oversight for AI-generated content to verify accuracy and minimize bias.

units.why: 'Protect intellectual property rights; avoid ... inputting journal articles or other copyrighted materials in non-enterprise tools' is a copyright rule (P52).
units.anchor: Protect intellectual property rights; avoid intentionally inputting journal articles or other copyrighted materials in non-enterprise
units.policy: Protect intellectual property rights; avoid intentionally inputting journal articles or other copyrighted materials in non-enterprise tools.
units.fit_note: Also limits inputs to non-enterprise tools, which P52 (licensing of inputs and outputs) only partly captures.

units.why: 'Verify AI output before accepting it as fact' directly states the P31 verification duty.
units.anchor: Verify AI output before accepting it as fact.

units.why: Asks users to 'generate content that encourages fair representation', a bias concern (P53).
units.anchor: Consistently edit, revise, and actively work to generate content that encourages fair representation.

units.why: States as fact that models 'may unintentionally perpetuate existing biases and inequalities'; it names a harm, so P53 with modality informs.
units.anchor: AI models are trained on datasets of historical information, images, and textual references that may
units.policy: AI models are trained on datasets of historical information, images, and textual references that may unintentionally perpetuate existing biases

units.why: Says users 'must be aware of and actively address' limitations and biases, a bias concern (P53); P31 is about checking output specifically.
units.anchor: AI tools come with inherent limitations and potential biases that users must be aware of
units.policy: AI tools come with inherent limitations and potential biases that users must be aware of and actively address

units.why: 'Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance' keeps people from letting AI replace their own thinking (P32).
units.anchor: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool
units.fit_note: Frames it as periodic self-evaluation, not only a rule about being the primary problem-solver.

units.why: 'Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated' is a disclosure duty (P24); P25 fits only partly because it asks for tool and manner of use but not the prompt or output.
units.anchor: Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, including what tool was used and how AI was
units.policy: Clearly disclose when content is AI-generated, including what tool was used and how AI was used
units.fit_note: Requires the tool and manner of use, not prompts or outputs as in P25.

units.why: 'Provide disclaimers up-front when AI will assist in decision-making' tells people they are dealing with AI (P103).
units.anchor: Provide disclaimers up-front when AI will assist in decision-making

units.why: Requires 'disclaimers for AI chat assistants' that state their limits, which is telling people they interact with AI and its limits (P103).
units.anchor: Provide disclaimers for AI chat assistants, informing users of the potential for incorrect information

units.why: Encourages using AI to make 'accessible materials ... screen-reader friendly documents', an accessibility aid (P97).
units.anchor: Use AI tools to create inclusive and accessible materials, such as multilingual content or screen-reader
units.policy: Use AI tools to create inclusive and accessible materials, such as multilingual content or screen-reader friendly documents

units.why: 'Advocate for equitable access ... free or university provided software' is the equity/access rule (P51).
units.anchor: Advocate for equitable access to AI tools across the university, including free or university provided
units.policy: Advocate for equitable access to AI tools across the university, including free or university provided software

units.why: 'Encourage ... to participate in AI Pilots on campus' is a push to join pilot programs; no type covers participation in campus pilots, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Encourage faculty, staff, and students to participate in AI Pilots on campus to explore AI
units.policy: Encourage faculty, staff, and students to participate in AI Pilots on campus to explore AI use.
units.uncovered_note: Encourages participation in campus AI pilots to explore AI use.

units.why: 'should complete the Generative AI Cybersecurity Awareness Bridge Training' is an institutional training recommended to all users (P70).
units.anchor: All users of free, paid (non-enterprise), or enterprise AI tools (university sanctioned) should complete the
units.policy: All users of free, paid (non-enterprise), or enterprise AI tools (university sanctioned) should complete the Generative AI Cybersecurity Awareness Bridge Training

units.why: 'Attend campus training sessions' on assessing AI output asks users to take institutional AI training (P70).
units.anchor: Attend campus training sessions to understand how to critically assess AI-generated output.

units.why: 'Familiarize yourself with the ethical implications ... and apply best practices' is a duty to stay informed (P102).
units.anchor: Familiarize yourself with the ethical implications of using AI in your role and apply best
units.policy: Familiarize yourself with the ethical implications of using AI in your role and apply best practices.
units.fit_note: Focuses on ethics and best practices rather than on developments or current guidance.

units.why: 'Recognize the rapid evolution of the AI tools and embrace a mindset of continuous learning' asks users to keep up with AI developments (P102).
units.anchor: Recognize the rapid evolution of the AI tools and embrace a mindset of continuous learning.

units.why: 'a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning' says AI must not replace the person's thinking (P32).
units.anchor: Recognize the use of AI as a tool, not a solution or replacement for work
units.policy: Recognize the use of AI as a tool, not a solution or replacement for work and/or learning.

units.why: 'Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI' asks the whole community to discuss AI; P66 is specifically instructors explaining rules to students, so I use UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI in addition to the ethics of
units.policy: Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI in addition to the ethics of using AI at the university.
units.uncovered_note: Asks that discussions of the benefits, limitations and ethics of AI be prioritized at the university.

documents.title: Faculty Guiding Principles
documents.summary: Principles for faculty on integrity, transparency, access and literacy. Instructors must set AI statements in syllabi and assignments, need student approval for AI grading, should not rely on detectors alone, and should disclose their own AI use.
documents.stance_why: The page tells faculty to 'Create a syllabus statement for each course' with their own stance and examples of permitted and prohibited use, so the course-level AI rule is left to each instructor. Its other guidance (AI grading needs student approval, detectors are not proof) does not set a stance on student AI use.

units.why: AI grading or feedback must be 'clearly stated in the syllabus' and have 'explicit approval from students', a condition on AI-assisted grading (P101); P47 (disclosure) does not capture the consent requirement.
units.anchor: Use of AI to grade or give feedback on assignments should be clearly stated in
units.policy: Use of AI to grade or give feedback on assignments should be clearly stated in the syllabus and have explicit approval from students

units.why: 'offer a human-alternative ... for those who do not consent' is a condition on AI-assisted grading (P101); P51 is about access to AI, not opt-out of AI grading.
units.anchor: Instructors should offer a human-alternative (e.g., teacher, TA) for those who do not consent
units.fit_note: Also an opt-out alternative for students, as in P51.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to grade assignments or input student work ... without prior approval' conditions AI grading on student approval, with a FERPA basis (P101; P46 would ban AI grading outright).
units.anchor: Do not use AI to grade assignments or input student work/information without prior approval from
units.policy: Do not use AI to grade assignments or input student work/information without prior approval from students

units.why: 'Ensure all data is deidentified' is a data-protection requirement addressed to faculty (P50).
units.anchor: Ensure all data is deidentified when using in an AI tool.

units.why: 'Prioritize using vetted UNO enterprise tools' means using university-approved tools, institution-wide (P92).
units.anchor: Prioritize using vetted UNO enterprise tools when using AI in your work.

units.why: Detector results are 'a starting point for discussion, not ... conclusive evidence', an evidence standard (P69); P39 does not fit exactly because detectors are not banned.
units.anchor: using these tools to identify violations of academic integrity should be a starting point for
units.policy: using these tools to identify violations of academic integrity should be a starting point for discussion, not as conclusive evidence
units.fit_note: Detector may still be used to start a conversation; P39 says detectors are not relied on.

units.why: 'should not rely solely on one accountability measurement' sets an evidence standard for misuse findings (P69).
units.anchor: All investigations into academic integrity should not rely solely on one accountability measurement

units.why: 'Ensure AI integration in your class promotes ethical and responsible use of AI' makes course AI integration answerable to an ethics goal; it is not a rule or a literacy duty that existing types describe, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Ensure AI integration in your class promotes ethical and responsible use of AI
units.uncovered_note: Instructors must ensure that any AI integration in their class promotes ethical and responsible use.

units.why: 'Provide students with citation or attribution guidelines for AI use' supports disclosure by telling students how to cite (P24).
units.anchor: Provide students with citation or attribution guidelines for AI use
units.fit_note: Addressed to instructors (supply guidelines) rather than students (must disclose).

units.why: 'fostering discussions about fairness and inclusion' means discussing AI in class with students (P66).
units.anchor: Address potential AI biases by fostering discussions about fairness and inclusion in its applications
units.fit_note: Topic is bias and fairness rather than the course's AI rules.

units.why: 'think critically about AI output; cross check results' is the verify-output duty (P31), here for faculty.
units.anchor: Always think critically about AI output; cross check results with web searches, or relevant places
units.policy: Always think critically about AI output; cross check results with web searches, or relevant places to ensure accuracy and reliability

units.why: 'analyze AI output for bias and stereotypes' is a duty to evaluate output critically (P31).
units.anchor: Always analyze AI output for bias and stereotypes to reduce potential harm in final output

units.why: 'Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance' keeps AI from replacing one's thinking (P32).
units.anchor: Regularly evaluate AI use to prevent an overreliance on the tool
units.fit_note: Periodic self-evaluation duty.

units.why: 'Create a syllabus statement for each course' requires an AI statement in every syllabus (P09).
units.anchor: Create a syllabus statement for each course

units.why: The syllabus statement must explain 'the instructor's stance on AI', so each instructor sets and states a stance (P04); P09 already used for the duty to have a statement.
units.anchor: An explanation of the instructor's stance on AI is for the course

units.why: The statement must give 'Clear examples of permitted and prohibited AI use', specifying what the syllabus must contain (P09).
units.anchor: Clear examples of permitted and prohibited AI use

units.why: The statement must state 'Potential consequences for unapproved uses', advance notice of penalties (P37).
units.anchor: Potential consequences for unapproved uses
units.fit_note: Requires naming consequences but does not state any concrete penalty.

units.why: 'Include AI use statements in assignments' for 'when and how AI is permitted or prohibited' requires assignment-level AI statements (P09).
units.anchor: Include AI use statements in assignments to provide clear guidance for when and how AI
units.policy: Include AI use statements in assignments to provide clear guidance for when and how AI is permitted or prohibited

units.why: Instructors should 'clearly state when AI assisted in the creation of an assignment, content, or course design', disclosure of instructor AI use (P47).
units.anchor: clearly state when AI assisted in the creation of an assignment, content, or course design

units.why: 'Clearly identify AI-generated materials' in course materials is disclosure of AI-made course materials (P48).
units.anchor: Clearly identify AI-generated materials (e.g., images) in lectures or other course materials

units.why: Tools used in class must be 'available to all students, regardless of ... financial resources', the equity rule (P51).
units.anchor: Ensure the AI tools used in class are available to all students, regardless of background
units.policy: Ensure the AI tools used in class are available to all students, regardless of background or financial resources

units.why: 'Regularly assess AI-generated course content' is review of AI-made course materials (P48).
units.anchor: Regularly assess AI-generated course content for fairness, accuracy, and inclusivity

units.why: Encourages instructors to 'adapt teaching materials for diverse learning needs' with AI, an instructor use for teaching work (P59); P97 is about accessibility of tools and output.
units.anchor: Use AI to adapt teaching materials for diverse learning needs (e.g., multilingual or accessible resources)
units.fit_note: Also an accessibility aim (P97).

units.why: 'attend workshops, webinars' is faculty learning support and expectation (P63).
units.anchor: Support and encourage continuous learning; attend workshops, webinars, etc.

units.why: 'AI-focused assignments that teach students how to be ethical and responsible users' means courses teach AI use (P44); P79 does not fit since AI use is not required for graded tasks.
units.anchor: Incorporate AI-focused assignments that teach students how to be ethical and responsible users and consumers
units.policy: Incorporate AI-focused assignments that teach students how to be ethical and responsible users and consumers of AI
units.fit_note: Teaches ethical use rather than professional skill specifically.

units.why: Instructors should 'offer explanations and lectures on AI capabilities and ethical considerations', courses that teach about AI (P44).
units.anchor: Offer explanations and lectures on AI capabilities and ethical considerations in your field
units.fit_note: Content is capabilities and ethics rather than professional-skill claims.

units.why: 'Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI' is a call for community discussion, not instructors explaining rules to students (P66), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI in addition to the ethics of
units.policy: Prioritize discussions about the benefits and limitations of AI in addition to the ethics of using AI in faculty roles
units.uncovered_note: Asks that discussions of the benefits, limitations and ethics of AI be prioritized at the university.

documents.title: Student Guiding Principles
documents.summary: Student principles under integrity, transparency, access and literacy. Students follow each course's AI statement, ask when unsure, disclose and verify AI use, protect course materials, report misuse, and may opt out of AI use.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'faculty have the ability to choose how and when they incorporate AI into their courses' and that students must follow each instructor's syllabus statement, so it sets no stance and hands the decision to instructors.

units.policy: Only use AI in accordance with the AI syllabus statement and/or AI use statements in your course(s)

units.policy: Always think critically about AI output; cross check results with course material, web searches, or relevant places

documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: UNO's university-wide academic integrity policy, revised in February 2026 to add AI language. AI use outside instructor authorization is cheating, students follow course AI statements and ask when unsure, and the default is no AI without approval. The rest of the policy covers general integrity procedures.
documents.stance_why: The policy lists 'Using software or AI during an exam or for an assignment that is not authorized by the instructor' as cheating and says 'Without explicit AI usage approval from the instructor, students should assume that AI may not be used', so AI is banned unless permitted.

units.why: Listed under 'Cheating': 'Using software or AI during an exam or for an assignment that is not authorized by the instructor' is classified as academic misconduct (P36); P22 would be a flat exam ban, which this is not.
units.anchor: Using software or AI during an exam or for an assignment that is not authorized
units.policy: Using software or AI during an exam or for an assignment that is not authorized by the instructor.

units.why: Students 'are expected to use AI tools in accordance with the AI use statements in the course syllabus', responsibility to follow each course's rules (P78).
units.anchor: Use AI tools in accordance with the AI use statements in the course syllabus

units.why: 'Seek clarification from the instructor in advance' when unsure is the ask-first rule (P10).
units.anchor: Seek clarification from the instructor in advance if there is any uncertainty regarding the permissibility
units.policy: Seek clarification from the instructor in advance if there is any uncertainty regarding the permissibility of AI use

units.why: 'Without explicit AI usage approval ... assume that AI may not be used for assignments or exams' is a fallback when a syllabus is silent (P06).
units.anchor: Without explicit AI usage approval from the instructor, students should assume that AI may not
units.policy: Without explicit AI usage approval from the instructor, students should assume that AI may not be used

units.why: The history says the revision 'approved by Senior Executive Leadership' added 'language regarding artificial intelligence', stating how and when the AI language was adopted (P84).

units.policy: Policy revision approved by Senior Executive Leadership. Primary revisions include addition of language regarding artificial intelligence

notes: General integrity procedures (reporting, mediation, appeal, repeat offenses) in the Academic Integrity Policy are not AI-specific and were not coded as units; they apply to AI misuse by implication. Prioritize-discussions and AI-pilot lines recur across the guiding-principles pages and were coded UNCOVERED; candidate new types: community discussion of AI benefits/limits; participation in campus AI pilots; no use of AI explanation to contest a grade.
